excerpts.text: In 1989, he proposed a global hypertext document system using the Internet, allowing researchers to share information online.

Tim Berners-Lee, a British computer scientist, is most famously known as the inventor of the [World Wide Web](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Tim-Berners-Lee/Introduction#ref1). In 1989, while at CERN, Berners-Lee proposed a global hypertext system to allow researchers to easily share their results and techniques.

In 1989, [Tim Berners-Lee](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Tim-Berners-Lee/Introduction#ref1) and his colleagues at CERN developed it, including the HyperText Transfer Protocol (HTTP) for standardized server-client communication.
